title: Army Weekly Briefing
description: Army leadership, force design, modernization, contracts and the signal and network enterprise.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 17–27. New: the Associated Press reported Nov. 27 that the EPA expects laboratory results from the Iowa lead-azide detonation to start arriving as early as Friday, and that airborne-lead monitors have continued to read zero since Wednesday. Dark Eagle fielding and the Guam terrain walk remain. No new NETCOM release was found. No new Army enterprise software agreement dated Nov. 26–27 was found in Army CIO reporting, ESI, war.gov, Federal News Network, Breaking Defense, DefenseScoop, Nextgov, GovConWire, or vendor newsrooms.

items.headline: EPA says Iowa lab results could start Friday; airborne lead still reads zero
items.summary: The Associated Press reported Nov. 27 that the EPA expects laboratory results from sampling after the Army's controlled detonation of the nation's lead-azide stockpile to start coming in as early as Friday. The EPA said in a Thursday statement, as reported by the Associated Press, that personnel and contractors took more than 1,500 samples of air, water, soil, and dust before the detonation and hundreds afterward, including from homes, parks, and drinking water, and that airborne-lead monitors have continued to read zero since Wednesday. The White House said Nov. 25 that the Army that morning destroyed nearly five tons of degraded explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant and that initial indications showed no secondary explosions or infrastructure damage. In that release, Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said the threat of an uncontrolled spontaneous detonation has been eliminated.

items.headline: Army publishes a guide for defending installation infrastructure with local partners
items.summary: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 23 that the Army published a Defense Critical Infrastructure Community Coordination Guide with CISA, the FBI, the EPA, the departments of Transportation and Energy, and FEMA. The guide is meant to help installations plan with the private companies and local governments that own the power, water, and communications systems Army units use to reach ports, rail, and airports. Lt. Gen. Matthew McFarlane, commander of I Corps, told reporters after a Joint Base Lewis-McChord summit that a disruption to a municipal power grid, a water system, or a fiber trunk is felt immediately by the mission. Brandon Pugh, principal cyber advisor to the Secretary of the Army, told reporters he hopes the guide will be scaled across the Army and the Department of War.

items.headline: Trump nominates Army Lt. Gen. Patrick Frank to lead NORTHCOM and NORAD
items.summary: DefenseScoop reported Nov. 19 that President Donald Trump nominated Army Lt. Gen. Patrick Frank to lead U.S. Northern Command and North American Aerospace Defense Command, and that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the nomination Wednesday. DefenseScoop said Frank would be promoted to general if the Senate confirms him, and that he has been U.S. Central Command's deputy commander since June. He would replace Air Force Gen. Gregory Guillot, who took the dual-hatted command in February 2024. DefenseScoop said the commands are modernizing against cruise missiles, drone incursions, and hypersonic threats and are moving toward software-defined, artificial-intelligence-enabled defense networks.

items.headline: Sutten assumes command of CECOM and Aberdeen Proving Ground
items.summary: Army.mil reported Nov. 17 that Brig. Gen. Marne L. Sutten assumed command of the Communications-Electronics Command and the duties of Aberdeen Proving Ground senior commander at a ceremony on Nov. 16. The article said she leads a 9,000-person global command and is senior commander of a 28,000-person installation, and that she is the Army's command, control, communications, computers, cyber, intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, and medical materiel integrator. Lt. Gen. Gavin A. Lawrence, deputy commanding general and acting commander of Army Materiel Command, presided and said Sutten most recently directed network command, control, cyber communications systems integration on the G-6. Sutten said she is the 19th commander of CECOM.

items.headline: Lozano says the first Dark Eagle battery is fully fielded
items.summary: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 25 that Lt. Gen. Frank Lozano, Program Acquisition Executive for Fires, said in a Nov. 19 interview that the Army's first Long Range Hypersonic Weapon battery, also called Dark Eagle, is fully fielded and ready to go. Lozano declined to say when or where it was fielded. Breaking Defense said the Army first planned to field the battery in 2023 and later missed a September 2025 target, and that Lozano said the service is already over halfway through production of the third battery. He said he would like two or three vendors in production against one requirement, and that a scaled hypersonics program is meant to fill the range gap between Dark Eagle and Castelion's Blackbeard.

items.headline: LaNeve's plan would replace Continuous Transformation by Feb. 1
items.summary: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 24 that Col. Pete Walther, a special assistant to Gen. Christopher LaNeve, said "How the Army Fights" is in the execute-order stage and is scheduled to become the Army's official campaign plan by Feb. 1, replacing "Continuous Transformation." Walther said Transformation in Contact and the Army Transformation Initiative are ending, not being rebranded, and that experimental technology for combat-training-center rotations will be directed from division level or above rather than by commanders at brigade and below. He said units must receive that equipment at least 180 days before a rotation, and that LaNeve wants battalions and below focused on close battle, strike at brigade and above, and convergence at division and above. A LaNeve spokesperson told Breaking Defense the change is meant to survive even if the Senate does not confirm him.

items.headline: Army air defenders walk Guam sites for a 360-degree missile defense
items.summary: Army.mil reported Nov. 26 that service members conducted a terrain walk on Guam from Nov. 17 to 19 to assess how the island could support the Guam Defense System. The article said the system is meant to provide 360-degree integrated air and missile defense against ballistic, hypersonic, and cruise missile threats, and that discussions covered sensor coverage, command and control, communications, and coordination across locations. Lt. Col. Joshua Urness, commander of 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defense Artillery Regiment, said walking the sites with Navy, Air Force, and Missile Defense Agency teammates showed how sensors and launchers become one defense. Brig. Gen. William Parker, commanding general of the 94th Army Air and Missile Defense Command, said the capability would defend the homeland and bring combat power forward.

items.headline: Army seeks power and data-center leases at nine installations
items.summary: Holland & Knight said Nov. 23 that the Army issued a request for proposals, dated Nov. 19 and announced Nov. 20, for enhanced-use leases at nine installations to develop commercial power generation, with an option to add a data center. The firm said the Army prefers integrated projects, will not consider data-center-only proposals, and will not commit to buy power or data-center capacity from a project. Military.com reported Nov. 24 that the notice requires power within one hour of a grid outage for at least 14 continuous days, describes an initial 25-year lease, requires water use to be net-neutral or better, and sets proposals due Jan. 18, 2027. The nine sites are Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Fort Bragg, Fort Hood, Fort McCoy, Fort Rucker, Blue Grass Army Depot, Pine Bluff Arsenal, Tooele Army Depot, and Sierra Army Depot.

items.headline: Army awards Sherpa 6 a $99.9 million tactical-edge endpoint contract
items.summary: Military Aerospace reported Nov. 20 that the Army awarded Sherpa 6 Inc. of Littleton, Colorado, a Small Business Innovation Research Phase III indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract valued at $99,878,455 to demonstrate a unified endpoint management platform at the tactical edge. Military Aerospace said Army Contracting Command at Aberdeen Proving Ground is the contracting activity and that the estimated completion date is Nov. 17, 2031. The company develops Watchtower, a platform for device provisioning, configuration, application distribution, and security enforcement in classified and unclassified enclaves. Military Aerospace said the Army announcement does not name Watchtower or say whether the effort buys that platform, adds development, or demonstrates a wider set of capabilities.

items.headline: Fort Belvoir team is folding the Odin planning app into NGC2
items.summary: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 24 that a team at the Army C5ISR Center at Fort Belvoir is building Odin, an artificial-intelligence-enhanced mission-planning app for battalion, company, and platoon. Maj. Andrew Durfee, who leads the team, said higher headquarters already have planning tools, while the tactical edge has less compute and bandwidth, and that Odin is being integrated into Next Generation Command and Control. He said the team has worked with Palantir and Anduril on data sharing, that earlier versions were tested by the 4th Infantry Division and at Project Convergence Capstone 6, and that the app can show where friendly sensors cannot see. Durfee said the team wants an AI course-of-action generator but is building a light version because that capability needs more processing than a junior officer can carry.

items.headline: CECOM's Aberdeen logistics center reports satellite training and a WIN-T cut
items.summary: Army.mil reported Nov. 20 that the Communications-Electronics Command Integrated Logistics Support Center, at Aberdeen Proving Ground, trained 4th Infantry Division soldiers and warrant officers on next-generation geostationary and low-Earth-orbit satellite systems. The center said its supply directorate eliminated $161 million in legacy Warfighter Information Network-Tactical forecasts across 50 major end items under the C2NOW program, and that it disposed of more than $1.4 billion in outdated parts. It said the Army Field Integrated Collaboration System, used with Army Vantage, gives warfighters real-time weapon-system data through automated pipelines and what the article called SI-powered searches. The center said its Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Maintenance tool was validated at the National Training Center and in a live use case at Project Convergence-Capstone 6.

items.headline: Army extends the Data Operations Center pilot to Oct. 1, 2027
items.summary: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 19 that Chad Nash, deputy of the Army Data Operations Center, said at the AFCEA Data Forum that the pilot is extended from Oct. 1, 2026, to Oct. 1, 2027 so the Army can keep measuring the volume of data problems it is clearing. Breaking Defense said the center was established in April as a 180-day pilot and help desk for formations, especially at the tactical edge, that could not get to their data. Col. Reginald Evans, director of the Command and Control Future Capability Directorate and the center, said the Army still would not have enough people to fill permanent billets and is relying on personnel borrowed from other organizations at Aberdeen Proving Ground. Nash said problems that took about two months at the start are now being solved in days, and that senior leaders will decide after the extension whether the center becomes permanent.
